gen-tourney-gf-questrial: Tourney cuts every stroke to a single width and stretches its words wide, with chunky little lowercase. Questrial offers sans letters with open, stencil-flat shapes, so extended reading stays smooth and light.
gen-tourney-gf-radio-canada: Tourney stretches wide, bulky letters cut in a single stroke width. Radio Canada, a sans with full lowercase c, s and z and open curve ends, keeps extended reading steady and current.
gen-tourney-gf-roboto: Roboto reads easily, its round letters generously open and its lowercase close to capital height. But Tourney's single-width strokes make the real difference, a bold, athletic shout over a sans-serif body.
gen-tourney-gf-savate: Savate has sturdy hairlines, open curves and a round o close to the capital's. And Tourney's unmodulated strokes leave it free to carry whole paragraphs gently with quiet contrast.
gen-tourney-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Schibsted Grotesk gives its e and a big, open bowls and terminals that never close in, against Tourney's neon-tube lines. Give its text a modest bump in size for comfort.
gen-tourney-gf-sen: Tourney draws every stroke at a single width, stretched wide and bulky. Sen's lowercase rises, traced in constant weight with open curve ends, a plain sans that echoes Tourney's monoline build.
gen-tourney-gf-sintony: Loud, stretched and bulky: that's Tourney up top. Sintony's chunky midzone and smooth, unclogged curves share Tourney's lack of stroke contrast, so the sans body feels built from the same stuff.
gen-tourney-gf-sofia-sans: Athletic from the first letter, Tourney stretches bold single-width strokes wide and bulky. Sofia Sans, with open-sided rounds and stencil-like lowercase, can take a slightly larger size than usual.
gen-tourney-gf-sofia-sans-semi-condensed: Sofia Sans Semi Condensed holds its lowercase near capital height, with a big visible entrance into each curve. Sofia Sans Semi Condensed reads smoothly in paragraphs, its constant stencil-channel weight leaving Tourney's bulk to shout.
gen-tourney-gf-sono: Sono spaces its letters generously, leaves each a ajar and lifts its lowercase high against the capitals. And Tourney's one-width strokes give that sans a loud partner, since both draw their lines with no swell.
